brief: 5 readability rules every designer breaks — and what to do instead in 2026.

slots.description: Inter is the definitive neo-grotesque screen font. Engineered for maximum legibility, it is the go-to choice for interface designers obsessed with clarity.
Cormorant Garamond is a dramatic, high-contrast serif family inspired by classic Garamonds. It excels in editorial layouts where generous line length lets its forms breathe.
Space Grotesk is a proportional sans-serif evolved from Space Mono. Its geometric frame and open apertures keep text crisp even in low-contrast palettes.
Fraunces is a variable serif with 'wonky' axes and soft serifs. Its dramatic weight range lets you build loud hierarchy without shouting.
Montserrat is a geometric sans inspired by Buenos Aires signage. Its tall x-height demands generous leading to prevent dense, suffocating blocks.
Instrument Serif is a refined transitional face with sharp details. Its narrow proportions reveal rivers and gaps when forced into careless justified settings.
DM Sans is a low-contrast neo-grotesque optimized for small screens. Its robust letterforms make it the ideal workhorse for accessible UI in 2026.

slots.body: Stop breaking these five rules and ship readable interfaces that actually convert in 2026.
